A1.justification: Both PDFs contain the same GradPower study, with complete, readable main text, Figures 1–7, Tables 1–2, and Appendices A–C. The substantive material can be reliably matched.

before.justification: v1 reports original language-model pre-training experiments in Section 3 and numerical simulations of stochastic gradient updates in Section 4.1.

after.justification: v2 retains the original pre-training experiments and gradient-update simulations, including their reported outcomes in Figures 1–7.

M1.justification: Section 2 and Algorithm 1 retain the same sign-power gradient transformation and AdamPower updates. Integration with Blockwise LR and Muon is also unchanged.

E1.justification: Both versions evaluate language-model pre-training on C4 and OpenWebText and the same synthetic gradient-noise example. No datasets, tasks, or distinct test scenarios are added or removed.

E2.justification: Adam, Adam with Blockwise LR, and Muon remain the evaluated baselines in their corresponding experiments. Figure 5 retains the same comparisons involving their GradPower variants.

E3.justification: Section 3 and Appendix A retain the same model configurations, training budgets, batch sizes, sequence lengths, learning-rate schedules, tuning procedures, and validation-loss evaluation. Tables 1–2 are unchanged.

E4.justification: The power sweep in Figure 2, batch-size analysis in Figure 6, and noise-regime simulation in Figure 7 are retained without additional or revised analyses.

E5.justification: Neither version reports experimental run or seed counts, confidence intervals, or significance tests. The figures and accompanying text retain the same uncertainty-reporting practices.

E6.justification: Figures 1–7 contain identical plotted results. The numerical comparisons and qualitative findings in Sections 3–4.1 also match; no result entries or reported outcomes change.

T1.justification: The mathematical definitions, assumptions, propositions, and convergence theorems remain unchanged. Appendices B–C retain the same derivations, lemmas, and proofs.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and conclusion retain the same claims about lightweight gradient transformation, improved pre-training performance, optimizer compatibility, and theoretical acceleration.

C2.justification: The interpretations concerning flat-direction progress, gradient noise, MoE stability, and warmup-stable-decay schedules are unchanged. The conclusion retains the same unresolved questions and proposed extensions beyond LLMs.

D1.justification: Appendix A retains the same tokenizer choices, architecture details, hyperparameters, tuning grids, and disclosure of eight A100 80G GPUs. No technical instructions or code/data access information are added or removed.

R1.justification: The cited works and research positioning are unchanged. Differences in bibliography back-reference page numbers follow the opening-page reflow and do not represent citation additions or removals.

P1.justification: v2 reverses the order of Jinbo Wang and Mingze Wang in the author list, adds the footnote 'This manuscript is currently under revision,' and makes a small punctuation edit. The scientific prose and section structure remain unchanged.

P2.justification: The additional first-page footnote causes limited reflow across pages 1–3, including a small shift of Figure 1. Figures 1–7 and Tables 1–2 retain their content and display structures.

improvement.justification: v2 changes author order and adds a manuscript-status note with minor layout adjustments. It preserves the methods, empirical evidence, theoretical arguments, interpretations, and reproducibility details, including the appendices, so no meaningful overall quality gain or loss is established.
